engineering_rationale: Iteration 1 passed legality, runtime, memory, and tail gates but failed the precommitted improvement threshold and reproducibility constraint. A readout-only step changes a permitted mutation class, avoids repeating the rejected learning-rate move, and reduces the trainable state that could contribute to run-to-run instability. This recommendation is gate-driven rather than post-hoc metric tuning and remains subordinate to legality, Tea Time, and evaluator decisions.
limitations: The recommendation uses aggregate metrics from one optimizer step and cannot establish generalization, uncertainty calibration, or scientific validity.
The validation set is reused, with no protected evaluation data or claim-bearing evidence.
The checkpoint remains candidate_only, and the recommendation cannot override legality, Tea Time, or evaluator gates.
risks: Readout-only training may be too restrictive to improve force MAE by the precommitted threshold.
The observed reproducibility failure may originate outside the trainable-layer scope, so this mutation may not reduce rerun_metric_delta.
Energy MAE per atom worsened slightly in iteration 1, and another update could deepen that tradeoff.
Reusing the same validation set makes further adaptation vulnerable to post-hoc selection bias; results must remain infrastructure-only.
scientific_rationale: Restricting adaptation to the readout preserves the candidate checkpoint's learned representation while testing whether a lower-capacity update can retain the small force-error improvement without increasing energy error. This is an infrastructure hypothesis only, not evidence of calibrated uncertainty or scientific superiority.
